A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ESC super-resolution work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, references, and supplementary material are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classic, arbitrary-scale, and real-world super-resolution evaluations, together with ablations, feature analyses, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds positional-encoding experiments, quantitative real-world evaluations, device benchmarks, and larger-model results.

M1.justification: The core ESC/ConvAttn procedure remains intact. The specified ESC-Real skip branch changes from a three-convolution sequence in v1 Section 6.3 to a sequence including LeakyReLU(0.2) in v2 Section 7.3. The added larger ESC variant also specifies extra normalization before ConvFFNs.

E1.justification: Real-world image coverage expands substantially: v1 evaluates RealSRSet, whereas v2 additionally evaluates RealLQ250, RealSR, and DRealSR (Section 9, Table 8). These introduce additional real-degraded image collections; the existing classic and arbitrary-scale benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 10 introduces comparisons against EDT-B, CAT-A, ART, ACT, and full-size SwinIR and SRFormer for the larger ESC model. This substantially extends the evaluated comparator set. The established lightweight and arbitrary-scale comparisons retain their methods; RealESRGAN's relabeling as RealESRGAN+ alone does not establish a new comparator.

E3.justification: ESC-Real's reported initial L1 training increases from 400K to 1M iterations; its subsequent 400K phase remains. New protocols include nine real-world quality metrics, MacBook/iPhone tests with different input sizes, and a 12.5M-parameter ESC using 48×48 attention windows and 64×64 pre-training followed by 96×96 fine-tuning. These are substantive setting additions and revisions.

E4.justification: v2 adds an isolated dynamic-kernel removal ablation (Table 3) and compares Flash Attention without positional encoding, with RoPE, and with relative positional bias (Table 6). Figure 6 replaces the ConvAttn inter-layer CKA analysis with kernel-specific gradient/receptive-field and input-wise similarity analyses. Figure 9 also replaces the building case with a dog example.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 100 repetitions for the existing GPU measurements. Neither introduces training-seed variability, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; the added results continue using point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, 4, 5, and the renumbered arbitrary-scale appendix table retain their numerical results. v2 adds substantial real-world, device, larger-model, and ablation results. For example, removing DK yields 33.36 versus ESC's 33.46 dB on Urban100×2, while Table 8 reports the highest CLIPIQA for ESC-Real on all four datasets. These additions are not longitudinal same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 4 corrects the fusion definition: v1 feeds F_fuse into its own defining concatenation, whereas v2 correctly uses F_res. This removes a circular mathematical definition and matches the existing prose description. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: replacing most self-attention with ConvAttn, integrating Flash Attention into lightweight SR, and preserving transformer-like representational capacity and data scalability. The headline performance and novelty claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2.4 shifts the mechanism interpretation from reduced inter-layer similarity to LK providing broader spatial influence and DK providing greater input-dependent diversity. The supplement additionally attributes Flash Attention training instability to missing relative positional bias and discusses applicability to constrained devices and larger models. These refine the existing scientific interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 identifies SwinIR-light as Figure 2's source, expands Flash Attention documentation, and supplies larger-model configurations and device/input specifications. Existing core training details and the code-access link remain. The new hidden-dimension disclosure is internally inconsistent: Section 7.1 assigns ESC-FP both 8 and 4, leaving that setting unresolved.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature supporting RoPE, real-world datasets and quality metrics, ConvFormer, and larger-model comparisons. Section 3.3 more explicitly distinguishes ConvAttn from attention-map sharing and large-kernel CNNs with pixel attention. The central research positioning and novelty claim remain stable.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact, with grammar corrections, terminology standardization, and localized rewrites. Flash Attention implementation discussion moves into an expanded supplementary section, existing supplementary sections are renumbered, and new evaluation sections are appended.

P2.justification: Figure 6 is substantially redesigned into feature, gradient, and input-similarity panels; Figure 9 replaces a visual example. Table 3 gains an ablation row, and new Tables 6 and 8–10 introduce several substantial displays. The original supplementary Table 6 becomes Table 7 and is relocated, rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: v1 supports its real-world claims mainly with selected visual examples and its deployment argument with GPU measurements. v2 substantially strengthens this evidence through four-dataset quantitative evaluation, MacBook/iPhone tests, and targeted controls for dynamic kernels and positional encoding. These address important gaps in empirical support while preserving the established benchmark results. The inconsistent hidden-dimension disclosure and metric-dependent real-world advantages limit the conclusions but do not outweigh the gains.
